title: Only 1 in 4 Japanese Adults Trust Social Media
paragraphs: Social media has become a major source of news for many people. However, according to a new survey in Japan, only about one in four adults trust the information they see there.

The nationwide survey was carried out by the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper and Waseda University's Institute for Advanced Social Sciences, and the results were reported in September 2026. Participants were asked how much they trusted information about political, social and other events that they obtained from social media platforms such as YouTube and X.

The survey found that 24% of respondents trusted such information, including those who said they trusted it "to some extent." In contrast, 74% said they did not trust it, including those who said they did not trust it at all.

There were clear differences between age groups. Young people were much more likely to trust social media. Among people aged 18 to 39, 38% said they trusted information on social media. This fell to 28% among people aged 40 to 59, and to just 14% among people aged 60 and older.

The survey also suggested that trust in social media may be linked to people's views on other issues. For example, 11% of all respondents agreed that the government can issue as many bonds as it needs to cover its deficit. However, among people who trusted social media, this figure rose to 23%, compared with 8% among those who did not trust it. Similarly, 12% of all respondents said that reducing greenhouse gases was unnecessary to deal with global warming, but this rose to 22% among people who trusted social media.

Other surveys in Japan have produced different numbers, depending on how the questions were asked. For instance, one 2026 analysis found that only about 11% of Japanese people trust social media for news. In addition, a separate survey of 1,200 people found that around 40% had experienced problems after trusting information on social media, and that television remains the most trusted source of information.
Concerns about social media are growing in Japan. Some experts have warned that false and extreme claims can spread easily on these platforms.
